A.explanation: Dividing $50$ by $20$ gives $2.5$ and dividing $20$ by $50$ gives $0.4$, but work is force multiplied by distance, not divided.

B.explanation: This is $50 / 20 = 2.5$, which reverses the work relationship and has no physical meaning for $20 \text{ N}$ acting over $50 \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: This is half the correct product, possibly from using $10 \text{ N}$ instead of $20 \text{ N}$ or halving $20 \times 50$ by mistake.

D.explanation: Work $= 20 \text{ N} \times 50 \text{ m} = 1000 \text{ N m} = 1000 \text{ J}$ for the force acting in the direction of motion over the whole length.

hints: Notice the diagram shows the $20 \text{ N}$ pull acting horizontally along the tape, in the same direction the $50 \text{ m}$ of tape moves as it unwraps.
Recall that work done by a constant force along the direction of motion is the product of force and distance moved, $W = Fx$.
Multiply $20 \text{ N}$ by $50 \text{ m}$ and check that $1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ J}$ to get the total work for the whole roll.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: constant pulling force $F = 20 \text{ N}$ and total distance the force moves $x = 50 \text{ m}$, equal to the length of tape.
State the governing rule: for a constant force in the direction of displacement, work done $W = Fx$.
Calculate the product: $20 \times 50 = 1000$, so $W = 1000 \text{ N m} = 1000 \text{ J}$.
The $1000 \text{ J}$ value matches the largest option. This is option D.
